ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Answer-likelihood gain as a turn reward for GRPO search agents
PROPOSAL: Define the reward of each turn as the change in the policy's log-probability of the ground-truth answer, evaluated by teacher-forcing the answer after the turn, and add it to the outcome reward after group normalization. Train Qwen2.5-7B on a mixed NQ and HotpotQA set in a Search-R1 style loop with a local Wikipedia retriever, 8 rollouts per query, up to 4 turns, a learning rate of 1e-6 and 256 queries per batch. Evaluate exact match on NQ, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, Musique and Bamboogle.
CONTROLS: Compare with outcome-only GRPO, a turn reward from an external judge on a subset, and a fixed-per-turn bonus; ablate the mixing weight; run 3 seeds for the main comparison.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: Exact match should improve by about 2 points over outcome-only training on multi-hop sets. It could fail if likelihood gain rewards turns that only echo the question, leaving final accuracy unchanged.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Likelihood-gain turn reward in GRPO training of search agents on three model sizes
PROPOSAL: Define the reward of each turn as the change in the policy's log-probability of the ground-truth answer, teacher-forced after the turn, and add it to the outcome reward after group normalization. Train Qwen2.5-3B, 7B and 14B on mixed NQ and HotpotQA data in a Search-R1 style loop with a local Wikipedia retriever, 8 rollouts per query and up to 4 turns, for 3 seeds each at 3 mixing weights. Evaluate exact match on NQ, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, Musique and Bamboogle at 5 checkpoints.
CONTROLS: Compare with outcome-only GRPO and a fixed-per-turn bonus; ablate the mixing weight; report the curves at each checkpoint by model size.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: Exact match should improve by about 2 points over outcome-only training on multi-hop sets. It could fail if the reward favors turns that echo the question, leaving final accuracy unchanged.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Turn-level advantage fallback when all rollouts in a group ties
PROPOSAL: When all rollouts of a query share the same outcome reward, replace the zero advantage with a normalized turn-level score: the rank of each rollout by mean gain in answer log-probability over its turns. Implement inside verl on Qwen2.5-7B with a local Wikipedia retriever, train on NQ and HotpotQA with 8 rollouts, 4 turns, batch size 256 and learning rate 1e-6, and log the share of groups with vanishing gradient together with exact match on NQ, HotpotQA, Musique and Bamboogle.
CONTROLS: Compare with outcome-only GRPO, dynamic sampling that discards tied groups, and a random tie-break advantage; ablate the rank normalization; use 3 seeds.
COST: 3200
PREDICTION: The share of groups with zero gradient should fall to under a tenth and exact match should rise by about 1.5 points. It could fail when tied groups are mostly unanswerable queries, where the fallback ranks noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Turn-level advantage fallback for tied groups with outcome rewards from four retrievers
PROPOSAL: When all rollouts of a query share the same outcome reward, replace the zero advantage with a normalized turn-level score: the rank of each rollout by mean gain in answer log-probability over its turns. Implement inside verl and train Qwen2.5 at three sizes with each of four retrievers (BM25, E5, BGE and a web search API cache) on NQ and HotpotQA with 8 rollouts and 4 turns, logging the share of groups with vanishing gradient and exact match on Musique, Bamboogle, NQ and HotpotQA at intervals of 50 steps.
CONTROLS: Compare with outcome-only GRPO and dynamic sampling that discards tied groups; ablate the rank normalization; use 3 seeds in each cell.
COST: 3200
PREDICTION: The share of groups with zero gradient should fall under a tenth and exact match should rise by about 1.5 points. It could fail when tied groups are mostly unanswerable queries, where the fallback ranks noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Does turn reward align with productive turns? A labeled audit of search trajectories
PROPOSAL: Sample 300 trajectories from a trained Qwen2.5-7B search agent on HotpotQA and Musique, and have two annotators mark each turn as productive when it retrieves a passage that supports a step of the reference reasoning chain. Correlate the answer-likelihood-gain reward with these labels per turn, and compare it with the correlation of a Monte Carlo rollout value estimate computed on a 50-trajectory subset. Report AUC, Spearman correlation and annotator agreement.
CONTROLS: Include a baseline using turn length, one using retrieval similarity to the question, and one shuffling turns within a trajectory; compute confidence intervals by bootstrap over queries.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: The turn reward should reach AUC near 0.75 for productive turns, above retrieval similarity. It could fail because early correct turns often show no likelihood gain until a later turn closes the chain.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Does turn reward track productive turns? Annotation study with rollout value estimates
PROPOSAL: Draw 300 trajectories from a trained Qwen2.5-7B search agent on HotpotQA and Musique and ask three annotators to label each turn as productive or not, using the reference reasoning chain. Estimate a Monte Carlo value for all turns of all trajectories from 16 continuations each, correlate it with the labels and with the answer-likelihood-gain reward, and report AUC, Spearman correlation and annotator agreement.
CONTROLS: Baselines are turn length and retrieval similarity; shuffled turn order is a null reference; bootstrap intervals are resampled over queries and over annotators.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: The turn reward should reach AUC near 0.75, above retrieval similarity. It could fail because early correct turns often show no gain until a later turn closes the chain.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reward hacking stress test for turn-level search rewards
PROPOSAL: Probe how a turn-level reward can be exploited by constructing adversarial policies: one that repeats searches returning answer-bearing passages, one that emits answer guesses in the reasoning text to raise likelihood, and one that issues empty tool calls. Train Qwen2.5-7B for 600 steps with reward clipping at 2.0, a cap of 3 rewarded turns per trajectory and a gain-over-previous-turn formulation, and test whether final-answer reward still tracks turn reward on held-out HotpotQA and Bamboogle queries. Track exact match, reward-accuracy correlation and mean turn count.
CONTROLS: Compare with outcome-only training and with an uncapped turn reward; vary the cap; add a variant that masks the reasoning text before computing likelihood.
COST: 5000
PREDICTION: Capped gain-based rewards should keep turn counts stable and correlation above 0.6, while the uncapped one should drift toward repetition. It could fail if drift appears only after longer training than we run.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reward hacking stress test for turn-level search rewards over long training runs
PROPOSAL: Probe how a turn-level reward can be exploited by constructing adversarial policies: one that repeats searches returning answer-bearing passages, one that places answer guesses in the reasoning text, and one that issues empty tool calls. Train Qwen2.5 at two sizes with reward clipping, a cap on rewarded turns and a gain-over-previous-turn formulation for 2000 steps, evaluating on HotpotQA, Musique, 2WikiMultiHopQA and Bamboogle at intervals of 100 steps. Track exact match, reward-accuracy correlation and mean turn count at each evaluation.
CONTROLS: Compare with outcome-only training and an uncapped turn reward; vary the cap over 5 values; mask the reasoning text before computing likelihood in one variant; repeat with 3 seeds.
COST: 5000
PREDICTION: Capped gain-based rewards should keep turn counts stable and correlation above 0.6, while the uncapped one should drift toward repetition. It could fail if drift only appears beyond the horizon we run.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Which models gain from dense turn supervision? Small and mid-sized models
PROPOSAL: Test the claim that weaker models gain most. Fine-tune Qwen2.5 instruction models of 1.5B, 3B and 7B parameters, each with outcome-only GRPO and with answer-likelihood-gain turn rewards under the same Search-R1 setup, 8 rollouts and 4 turns on NQ and HotpotQA with a local retriever. Report the exact-match gain from turn rewards on five test sets as a function of model size and of baseline outcome-reward success rate on the training queries.
CONTROLS: Compare with a base-model initialization and an instruction-model initialization; keep the data order identical across arms; run 3 seeds per cell; report the share of tied groups.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Gain should be larger for the 1.5B model than for 7B, with the tied-group share explaining part of it. It could fail if the smallest model cannot issue valid tool calls, so neither arm learns.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Which models gain from dense turn supervision? Qwen2.5 sizes and initializations
PROPOSAL: Test the claim that weaker models gain most. Starting from base and instruction checkpoints of Qwen2.5 at five sizes (1.5B to 32B), run outcome-only GRPO and GRPO with answer-likelihood-gain turn rewards in the Search-R1 setup, 8 rollouts, 4 turns, NQ and HotpotQA questions, local retriever. Report the exact-match gain from turn rewards on five test sets as a function of model size and of baseline success rate on training queries.
CONTROLS: Keep data order identical across arms; run 3 seeds per cell; report the share of tied groups per model and initialization.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Gain should be larger for the 1.5B model than for the biggest ones, with tied groups explaining part of it. It could fail if the smallest model cannot issue valid tool calls, so neither arm learns.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sample-efficiency curves for turn-rewarded versus outcome-only search agents
PROPOSAL: Compare how many sampled trajectories each method needs to reach a target accuracy. Train Qwen2.5-7B on HotpotQA with outcome-only GRPO and with a turn-level reward under identical batch sizes of 128 queries, and evaluate on a fixed 1000-query development set at intervals of 25 steps with 4 rollouts. Report trajectories-to-threshold for dev exact match at 0.35 and 0.40, area under the learning curve, and final test exact match on Musique and 2WikiMultiHopQA.
CONTROLS: Use matched learning rates for both arms plus a variant with outcome-only training and double the rollouts per query; run 3 seeds; report bootstrap intervals over seeds.
COST: 640
PREDICTION: The turn-level arm should reach the 0.40 threshold with about 30 percent fewer trajectories. It could fail if the advantage disappears once outcome-only training is tuned with more rollouts per query.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sample-efficiency curves for turn-rewarded and outcome-only agents under tuned settings
PROPOSAL: Compare how many sampled trajectories each method needs to reach a target accuracy. Train Qwen2.5-7B on HotpotQA with outcome-only GRPO and a turn-level reward under identical batch sizes, with five batch sizes and four learning rates per arm, evaluating on a fixed 1000-query development set at intervals of 25 steps. Report trajectories-to-threshold at 0.35 and 0.40, area under the learning curve and final test exact match on Musique and 2WikiMultiHopQA.
CONTROLS: Include an outcome-only variant with double the rollouts per query; run 3 seeds per configuration; report bootstrap intervals over seeds.
COST: 640
PREDICTION: The turn-level arm should reach the 0.40 threshold with about 30 percent fewer trajectories. It could fail if the advantage disappears once outcome-only training is tuned with more rollouts.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Measuring compute overhead of turn-level rewards in group-based optimization
PROPOSAL: Quantify the added cost of computing answer-likelihood-gain rewards. Instrument verl training of Qwen2.5-7B with 8 rollouts, 4 turns and 256 queries per batch, timing the extra teacher-forced forward passes per turn, the reward computation and the whole step, and compare with outcome-only steps on identical hardware. Test a batched implementation that reuses the cached prefix of each trajectory, and report relative overhead and memory use as a function of trajectory length.
CONTROLS: Compare with outcome-only steps and with an unbatched implementation; confirm identical rewards between implementations on 500 trajectories; repeat timings over 3 runs.
COST: 1400
PREDICTION: Batched prefix reuse should keep overhead under 10 percent of step time. It could fail for long trajectories where the answer scoring pass competes with generation for memory.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Measuring compute overhead of turn-level rewards for different model sizes and contexts
PROPOSAL: Quantify the added cost of computing answer-likelihood-gain rewards. Instrument verl training of Qwen2.5 at three sizes with 8 rollouts and turn limits of 2, 4 and 6, timing the extra teacher-forced forward passes per turn, the reward computation and the whole step, and compare with outcome-only steps on identical hardware. Test batched and unbatched implementations at 4 context lengths, and report relative overhead and memory use in each combination.
CONTROLS: Compare with outcome-only steps; confirm identical rewards between implementations on 500 trajectories; repeat timings over 3 runs in each cell.
COST: 1400
PREDICTION: Batched prefix reuse should keep overhead under 10 percent of step time. It could fail for long contexts where the answer scoring pass competes with generation for memory.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training on NQ and HotpotQA, testing out of domain: does turn supervision transfer?
PROPOSAL: Train Qwen2.5-7B search agents with outcome-only and with turn-level rewards on a mix of NQ and HotpotQA with 8 rollouts, 4 turns and 3 seeds, and test on 2WikiMultiHopQA, Musique, Bamboogle, TriviaQA and PopQA using the same retriever, plus a swap to a web search API cache not seen in training. Report exact match, mean number of search calls and fraction of trajectories that end without an answer in each condition.
CONTROLS: Compare with prompt-only workflow and supervised fine-tuning on trajectories from a stronger model; train 3 seeds; test the retriever swap on the same checkpoints.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: Turn-level training should keep its gain on out-of-domain sets, about 1 to 2 points, and degrade less under the retriever swap. It could fail if gains come from learning the training retriever's idiosyncrasies.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training on NQ and HotpotQA, testing out of domain with five retrievers and four models
PROPOSAL: Train Qwen2.5-7B search agents with outcome-only and with turn-level rewards on a mix of NQ and HotpotQA, and test on 2WikiMultiHopQA, Musique, Bamboogle, TriviaQA and PopQA with five retrievers, including a web search API cache not seen in training, and repeat the full training with Llama-3.1-8B and Mistral-7B. Report exact match, mean number of search calls and the fraction of trajectories ending without an answer in each condition.
CONTROLS: Compare with a prompt-only workflow and supervised fine-tuning on trajectories from a stronger model; train 3 seeds in each cell.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: Turn-level training should keep its gain on out-of-domain sets, about 1 to 2 points, and degrade less under retriever swaps. It could fail if gains come from learning the training retriever's idiosyncrasies.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Mixing weight and normalization choices for turn-level rewards
PROPOSAL: Study how turn rewards should be combined with the outcome reward. Train Qwen2.5-7B on NQ and HotpotQA with three schemes: add the group-normalized turn reward to the outcome advantage, normalize turn rewards within each turn index across the group, and scale turn rewards by the outcome reward sign. Sweep the weight over 0.1, 0.3 and 1.0 for the first scheme. Report exact match on five test sets, advantage variance and the fraction of rollouts whose advantage sign disagrees with outcome.
CONTROLS: Compare with outcome-only GRPO and turn-only training; run 2 seeds per cell; track whether the final-answer objective stays the dominant signal.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: The weight of 0.3 should balance gain and stability, and turn-only training should drift from final accuracy. It could fail if differences between schemes sit inside seed noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Weight schedules for combining turn rewards with outcome rewards
PROPOSAL: Examine whether the turn reward should fade during training. Fine-tune Qwen2.5-7B at a learning rate of 1e-6 on 5 training mixes of NQ and HotpotQA with a constant weight, a linear decay to zero and a cosine decay, plus a variant that raises the weight only for queries whose group tied on outcome. Search 8 initial weights per schedule and read out exact match on 5 test sets, how often turn advantages flip the sign of outcome advantages, and the entropy of the policy over training.
CONTROLS: Compare with outcome-only GRPO and turn-only training; run 3 seeds per cell; track whether the final-answer objective stays the dominant signal.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: Decay schedules should keep early guidance and end near outcome-only behavior, preserving final accuracy. It could fail if differences between schedules sit inside seed noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Answer-string presence versus likelihood gain as a cheap turn signal
PROPOSAL: Compare two inexpensive turn-level signals that need only question-answer pairs: a binary reward when a retrieved passage contains the ground-truth answer string, and the answer-likelihood gain. Train Qwen2.5-7B on HotpotQA with 8 rollouts and 4 turns under each signal, alone and combined with the outcome advantage, and evaluate on Musique, 2WikiMultiHopQA and Bamboogle. Report exact match, retrieval recall of supporting passages and the correlation between the two signals per turn.
CONTROLS: Compare with outcome-only GRPO and a reward from passage similarity to the question; check string matching with alias lists on 200 answers; use 3 seeds.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: Likelihood gain should beat string presence by about a point because aliases and partial matches break the string signal. It could fail if both signals correlate highly and the extra cost buys nothing.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gold-string hits and answer-probability gain: two cheap turn signals tested at different retrieval depths
PROPOSAL: Contrast two turn signals that need nothing beyond question-answer pairs: a binary hit when a fetched passage contains the ground-truth string, and the rise in answer probability after the turn. Train Qwen2.5-7B on HotpotQA with 8 rollouts and 4 turns using each signal alone or added to the outcome advantage, with the retriever returning from one to ten passages per call. Measure exact match on Musique, 2WikiMultiHopQA and Bamboogle, supporting-passage recall and how the two signals agree turn by turn.
CONTROLS: Baselines are outcome-only GRPO and passage-to-question similarity as reward; alias lists are checked on 200 answers; three seeds per setting.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: Probability gain should beat string hits by around a point since aliases break string matching. It could fail if the signals agree closely, so the costlier one buys nothing.
